evidence.description: 163 of 418 datasets in the 2026-09-13 catalogue measurement (39.0%) showed stale status with HTTP 200. HTTP 200 does not imply freshness across BNM, DOSM, exchequer, hansard, GTFS, NPRA, and others; consumers checking only HTTP status would misread a substantial group of stale datasets as fresh.
evidence.remeasurement_justification: The baseline moved because the catalogue genuinely freshened, not because detection was weakened. Comparing the committed 2026-09-05 snapshot (rev 01f1efdde, stale 180) with the 2026-09-13 measurement (stale 163): 21 datasets left stale (15 to aging, 6 to fresh), while only 4 entered stale (2 from aging, 1 from fresh, 1 from unknown-freshness). Healthy statuses also increased: fresh 94 -> 105 and aging 111 -> 124. The catalogue grew from 412 to 418 datasets. Movement in both directions shows detection is still classifying normally while datasets are moving to better statuses.

impact_on_claim_or_decision: Consumers checking only HTTP status would misread a substantial group of stale datasets as fresh.
resolution_or_quarantine: Per-family source cards document local staleness; consumers must inspect content_date.
rule_or_policy_change: Probe rule is correct; this record locks the corpus-level baseline.

regression_test.description: The observed stale-HTTP-200 percentage must stay within five points of the baseline.
